"Revelation First" most commonly refers to an emerging scholarly and theological argument that the Book of Revelation was actually the first book written in the New Testament. This challenges the traditional belief that Paul's epistles or the gospels were written first, claiming instead that John's apocalyptic vision serves as the foundation from which the rest of the New Testament unfolded. [1] The thesis—often associated with writers like Lee Sharks—revolves around several key points: * The "First & Last" Theme: In Revelation 1:11, Jesus declares "I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last," a theme some scholars argue profoundly shaped John’s later Gospel and epistles. [[1], [2]] * Inferential Timeline: It argues that traditional dating of New Testament books relies heavily on inferential settlements rather than direct historical fact, opening the door for Revelation’s texts to be dated earlier than 70 AD. [1] * Theological Seedbed: Proponents suggest that later New Testament theology unfolds as a transformation of the apocalyptic imagery originally introduced in Revelation. [1] Understanding the book of Revelation requires recognizing it as a genre of apocalyptic literature (a Greek word meaning "unveiling" or "disclosure") rather than just a disaster manual or secret code. It was originally written as a pastoral message to early Christians in Asia Minor facing persecution and spiritual apathy. [[1], [2], [3], [4]] To explore the nuances of this dating debate and the context of the text, you can review these resources: * Read the full essay outlining the argument on [Medium](https://medium.com/@leesharks00/revelation-first-revelation-early-the-apocalypse-as-the-earliest-new-testament-document-b0710fc55b73). * Dive into [Seattle Pacific University](https://spu.edu/lectio/prologue-to-scriptures-conclusion/) to learn more about the literary definitions of apocalypse in scripture. * Explore a theological breakdown on [Enduring Word](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-1/) for deeper context on Revelation 1. [[1], [2], [3]] Would you like to know more about the historical dating arguments used to support the Revelation First theory, or are you more interested in the pastoral and historical context of John's letters to the early churches?
